text:
morgan: Rolling the CUDA/Toolkit 11.x -> 12.2 images into eu-west GPU pool now. Seeing some nodes start failing pods with linker/runtime errors and nvlink flaps. Anyone seeing energy here?

aisha: Yup — eu-west-gpu-pool-2 has ~8 nodes flapping, pods restarting with a bunch of ld errors. Example from one pod: 
```
ld-linux-x86-64.so.2: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so
/opt/app/bin/service: relocation error: /usr/local/lib/libcudart.so.12: symbol __cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd, version CUDA_12 not defined in file libcuda.so with link time reference
```

chao: dmesg on the node shows NV driver/NVLink churn too: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 79` repeated and `nvlink: link reinitialize` messages. NCCL ops start timing out, rank init fails: `ncclCommInitRank returned unhandled system error`

infra-bot: [alert] 1745001250 - Node eu-west-asm-022 moved to NotReady (kernel tainted during module load).

liam: Wait — we also bumped the host gcc toolchain to 13 on that pool during last week's infra upgrade. Could be runtime ABI mismatch between container-compiled libs and host libstdc++/ld.

david-sre: I think so. Seeing symbol lookup/ABI mismatch in container logs: `undefined symbol: _ZNKSt8__detail15_List_node_base6M_hookEv` when libc++ interops with libstdc++. Container built against CUDA runtime from toolkit12 but host driver/libcuda is older on some nodes -> mixed symbols.

morgan: We did a partial image rebuild to include /usr/local/cuda/lib64 runtime stubs, but the rebuild queue is huge (120 images) and the orchestrator is slow — some services still run old images. Rebuild fallout + host toolchain change seems like a bad combo. Cost of repeatedly rebuilding is non-trivial too.

chao: Short-term mitigation: pin driver on affected nodes to 535.x (matches container runtime) and mark them as canary for rollback. Longer-term we either fully align host driver/toolchain + runtime libs, or keep containers fully self-contained (static-ish).

ross: We should cordon and drain affected nodes and shift workloads to us-east-dedicated where capacity exists. Can ops route noisy jobs away? Also need to surface to product if throughput impacted.

aisha: Action items I propose: 1) Cordon/drain the 8 flapping nodes (in progress), 2) Launch coordinated image rebuilds for top-20 critical services using new toolkit12 runtime (priority), 3) Roll host gcc back on a single canary node and test with rebuilt images, 4) Add node-setup modprobe retries and clearer logging so we can detect nvlink init failures earlier. :white_check_mark:

liam: Agree. Also add a preflight check to our provisioner that verifies libcuda.so version vs container cuda runtime version and fails fast with clear message.

david-sre: I'll instrument a quick debug job to exercise NCCL init across canary nodes so we catch rank init errors before we route traffic.

morgan: I'll open infra-ticket #INFRA-4892 with the rollback plan and schedule canary at 23:00 UTC. Tagging @oncall for the window.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: infra-rollback-canary -> 2025-03-12 23:00 UTC, nodes: eu-west-asm-020..027.

morgan: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If anyone sees more nodes start behaving like this, ping me directly. :pray:
